channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: O saldo nas redes para Lula e Flávio após o novo tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: An Agora Comunicação e Public Affairs analysis revealed that the new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products generated more negative social media mentions for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (280,000) than for President Lula (213,000), despite nearly identical negative sentiment levels (68.6% vs. 68.0%). Criticism of Flávio is dispersed across multiple actors, including Lula and allies, while his defense is largely self-generated, making it easier to caricature. The report highlights greater risk for Flávio due to his family’s ties to Donald Trump, but warns Lula also faces electoral limits in defending national sovereignty amid the tariffs.

item.title: Casado: Candidatura de Flávio é questionada por apoiadores após tarifaço
item.description: The 25% tariff imposed by the United States on Brazilian products is directly impacting Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, causing allies to question the viability of his candidacy, according to Letícia Casado on UOL News.

item.title: Ex-aliado cobra “exame toxicológico” de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Former federal deputy Julian Lemos, ex-coordinator of Jair Bolsonaro’s 2018 campaign in Paraíba, challenged Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to take a toxicology test and publish the results, implying drug use. The post on X (formerly Twitter) sparked controversy among Bolsonaro allies.

item.title: Governo e oposição trocam críticas após novas tarifas dos EUA
item.description: The Brazilian government and its allies accused the United States of imposing a 25% tariff on Brazilian exports as retaliation for alleged unfair trade practices, linking the measure to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and the Trump administration. The opposition criticized Lula’s foreign policy as ideologically driven and ineffective, claiming it provoked the U.S. response. Both sides announced countermeasures, with the government pledging to use the Reciprocity Law and WTO instruments to defend national interests.

item.title: Renan Santos atribui cancelamento de show à "sabotagem da esquerda"
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pré-candidate for the Missão party and lead singer of the band Limão Rosa, blamed the cancellation of a show at Audio Rebel in Botafogo (RJ) on a "sabotage" by the left, after the venue stated it did not want to risk associating its brand with a political figure in pre-campaign. Santos criticized the public’s reaction and claimed the cancellation resulted from social media pressure, insisting his band only sings about existential and relationship themes, not politics.

item.title: Flávio culpa Lula pelo tarifaço por desespero com Master, diz Guimarães
item.description: Minister José Guimarães accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of acting as a U.S. lobbyist and traitor to the nation for blaming Lula over the U.S. 25% tariff on Brazilian exports, linking his rhetoric to the Banco Master scandal and alleged ties to Daniel Vorcaro and 'Sicario'.

item.title: A vassalagem do clã Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro was accused of showing vassalage to the United States by using a USTR public hearing to attack the Lula government, advocate for tariffs on Brazilian products, and suggest the Trump administration wait for the 2026 elections to negotiate with a future president aligned with Washington, in alleged continuation of the coup attempt led by his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Presente de grego
item.description: Congress approved a special retirement benefit for 400,000 community health agents, creating an estimated annual cost of 2.7 billion reais over a decade without designated funding, prompting the economic team to consider a Supreme Court challenge. Senator Davi Alcolumbre, Senate President, is in a cold war with President Lula over parliamentary amendments, which have resurfaced following actions by Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino. While Congress is in recess, the STF is set to rule on budgetary obligations imposed on governors and review the constitutionality of parliamentary amendments, potentially reshaping Executive-Legislative dynamics.

item.title: Pré-candidatos à Presidência reagem a novo tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates reacted to the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazil, with Flávio Bolsonaro and Romeu Zema blaming Lula for provoking the measure, while Ronaldo Caiado criticized the Bolsonaros for their actions in the U.S. The Brazilian government rejected the tariff, citing the U.S. trade surplus with Brazil and claiming uninterrupted negotiations with the USTR, while also attributing the outcome of investigations to the Bolsonaro family's electoral motives.

item.title: Com novo tarifaço, governo Lula apostará em defesa da soberania e responsabilização de Flávio
item.description: The Lula government is maintaining a stance of national sovereignty defense against the new U.S. tariffs, avoiding political provocations and focusing on technical negotiations to expand exemptions. Meanwhile, Lula’s allies believe voters already associate the tariffs with Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL’s presidential pre-candidate, and see an opportunity to politically hold him accountable, leveraging public perception that he is the true architect behind Trump’s trade measures.

item.title: A partir de segunda (20), fica vedada a atuação de parentes de candidatos na Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: Starting Monday (20), relatives of candidates are prohibited from participating in electoral justice activities throughout the 2026 electoral period, from party conventions to the certification of elected officials. The restriction applies to judges, electoral tribunal members, auxiliaries, and court clerks who are spouses, partners, or relatives up to the second degree of registered candidates in the locality. The rule aims to ensure impartiality and is established in the Electoral Code and TSE Resolution No. 23.608/2019.

item.title: Nunes Marques diz que TSE aplicará normas contra robôs, cobra ação preventiva das big techs e rejeita limitação do debate político
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques announced that Brazil's Electoral Justice will implement a preventive model against abuses in the 2026 elections, targeting bots, AI-generated content, and digital disinformation. He emphasized that cooperation with platforms such as Meta, TikTok, and OpenAI aims to strengthen public trust in the electoral process without censoring political debate or restricting freedom of expression. Five memorandums of understanding were signed with platforms and three with AI companies to establish rapid, coordinated response protocols.

item.title: ‘Disputa entre Trump e Lula’: como a imprensa internacional repercutiu tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The U.S. announced a 25% tariff on select Brazilian imports, including ethanol, agricultural machinery and paper, effective July 22, following a USTR investigation that cited Brazilian policies as harmful to American interests. The measure, which exempts strategic goods like coffee, beef and oil, was widely covered in international media as a potential factor in Brazil’s October presidential election, with Lula blaming the Bolsonaro family for the threat and analysts suggesting the tariff could serve as an electoral boon for him.

item.title: Declarações dos EUA sobre pix são descabidas, diz governo Lula
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira dismissed U.S. claims that Pix constitutes an unfair trade practice, calling them 'baseless'. He stated the new 25% tariff on Brazilian goods lacks substance and is politically motivated, following over 30 meetings between the two governments since March 2025.

item.title: Em meio ao tarifaço, Flávio lança plano para mulheres em live nesta quinta
item.description: Despite the 25% tariff imposed by the United States on Brazilian goods dominating national political and economic debate, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, is maintaining his pre-campaign schedule and will hold a live stream at 7 p.m. this Thursday (16) targeting female voters, where he will unveil a specific plan for women. The broadcast will take place on his official channel amid the tense economic climate triggered by the new trade measures.

item.title: Menções a ‘Sicário’ crescem 1.240 vezes nas redes após foto com Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A photo of Flávio Bolsonaro alongside Luiz Phillipi Mourão, known as 'Sicário' and identified by the Federal Police as the leader of a private militia linked to banker Daniel Vorcaro, caused mentions of the term 'Sicário' on social media to surge 1,240 times within 24 hours. The analysis covered Instagram, X, and Facebook, with 80% of mentions tied to the candidate. Mourão was arrested in Operation Compliance Zero, attempted suicide in custody, and was later declared brain dead.

item.title: Edinho reúne ministros e cobra defesa do governo Lula nas redes
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva convened 11 Lula government ministers in Brasília to guide social media defense of the administration and warn about electoral blackout restrictions. The meeting underscores the PT’s strategy for Lula’s first-round re-election, emphasizing the alleged weakness of pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, labeled a 'sellout' due to his ties with Donald Trump.

item.title: Figueiredo rebate Caiado após crítica a Flávio: “Deveria estar ajudando”
item.description: Journalist Paulo Figueiredo rebutted former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado's criticism of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's trip to the United States, saying Caiado should be helping instead of attacking. Figueiredo argued the trip aimed to delay U.S. tariffs until after Brazil's elections, not cancel them, and accused Caiado of spreading misinformation. The exchange highlights growing tensions among Bolsonaro allies over foreign policy strategy toward the U.S.

item.title: Em aceno ao governo Lula, Câmara aprova R$ 1 bi de crédito extraordinário
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved six Provisional Measures releasing R$1.09 billion in extraordinary credits to President Lula's government. The funds still require Senate approval to take effect.

item.title: Eleições e resistência no Senado prejudicam propostas no Congresso: parlamentares entram em recesso sem votar fim da 6x1, PEC da Segurança e fim da taxa das blusinhas
item.description: Congress entered recess without voting on key proposals including the end of the 6x1 work schedule, the Security PEC, the MP to abolish the 'blusinhas tax', and the critical minerals exploration bill. The stall is mainly in the Senate, where President Davi Alcolumbre has clashed with the government, especially after blocking Jorge Messias’ STF nomination. The government hopes a meeting between Lula and Alcolumbre will unblock the agenda, particularly the repeal of the import tax on goods under US$ 50, seen as a move to boost Lula’s popularity ahead of his re-election bid.

item.title: Deputado do PT leva multa por retratar Tarcísio como Chucky
item.description: Deputy Emídio de Souza (PT-SP) was fined R$10,000 by the TRE-SP for a video portraying Governor Tarcísio de Freitas as the horror character Chucky, linking him to extreme violence in a political context. The court ruled the video constituted negative electoral propaganda and improper use of AI, ordering its removal. Souza said he will appeal, calling the decision an attempt to silence political criticism.

item.title: Moraes assume presidência do STF durante recesso e decidirá sobre questões urgentes
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes will assume the presidency of the STF (Supreme Federal Court) starting this Friday (17) and will serve in that role until the end of the judicial recess on July 31. During this period, he will be responsible for ruling on urgent matters, as stipulated by the court's internal regulations.

item.title: Caiado atribui peso do tarifaço dos EUA à polarização entre Lula e Flávio
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) attributed part of the responsibility for the tariff announcement by the Donald Trump U.S. government to the polarization between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Caiado stated that both contributed to an environment of instability that facilitated protectionist measures by the U.S. He argued that Brazil’s foreign policy needs more balance and less ideological polarization to avoid commercial retaliation.

item.title: Projeto destina recursos a programa de aprimoramento da gestão fiscal
item.description: The National Congress will analyze PLN 4/2026, proposing a supplementary credit of R$240 million for the Ministry of Finance. The funds will be used to implement technological solutions arising from the tax reform, through the Fiscal Management Modernization Program (Profisco III). The project, submitted by the Presidency of the Republic, awaits the appointment of a rapporteur in the Joint Budget Committee (CMO) before proceeding to a joint session vote in Congress.

item.title: Mauro Vieira: "O que incomoda os EUA é o Brasil não ter se curvado"
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated that the U.S. is bothered by Brazil's refusal to yield to excessive and unreasonable demands, including full and exclusive market access for U.S. firms without reciprocity. He rejected Secretary of State Marco Rubio's claims that Lula acted in bad faith during trade talks, noting the U.S. holds a $7.5 billion trade surplus with Brazil. Vieira defended Brazil's PIX system and called the new U.S. tariffs politically motivated and unjustified.

item.title: Vorcaro é questionado sobre foto de Flávio Bolsonaro com Sicário
item.description: Banker Daniel Vorcaro, detained at Papudinha, was questioned by his defense regarding a photo showing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro alongside Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as 'Sicário', identified by the Federal Police as head of Vorcaro's private militia. Vorcaro reportedly stated he did not know where the photo was taken, while Bolsonaro's allies downplay its impact, noting the senator routinely receives dozens of photo requests daily and cannot identify each individual. The image, published by journalist Juliana Dal Piva of ICL, sparked online discussion, though Bolsonaro's campaign dismisses it as random and devoid of personal significance.

item.title: Clécio anuncia que Teles Jr. fica na vice e fecha chapa no Amapá
item.description: Amapá Governor Clécio Luís (União Brasil) announced that Teles Jr. (PDT) will remain his running mate for re-election, abandoning plans for Teles to run for Senate. The Senate seat will be contested by the state deputy and president of the Legislative Assembly, while Senator Randolfe Rodrigues (PT) seeks re-election. The ticket is coordinated by the political group led by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil), who is not running this year due to his ongoing eight-year term.

item.title: Crusoé: Vieira acusa Rubio de ‘atacar’ Lula ao justificar tarifaço
item.description: Brazil's Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira criticized U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio for justifying a new 25% tariff on Brazilian goods via social media, calling the remarks 'rude and arrogant.' Vieira stated that Rubio had 'attacked' President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the leader of a friendly nation. The diplomatic strain arises amid renewed U.S. trade measures impacting Brazilian exports.

item.title: Tarifaço é bem pior para Flávio do que parece
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio blamed President Lula for the new U.S. tariff increase on approximately 3,000 Brazilian exports, citing a lack of good-faith negotiations. However, the bulk of the economic burden from the 25% surcharge falls on Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula’s main political rival, due to his ties with affected export sectors. The tariff measure creates a political dilemma for the opposition, which now faces direct consequences from a foreign policy outcome attributed to the Lula administration.

item.title: Governo Lula diz que EUA exigiram “capitulação” para rever tarifas
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated that the U.S. demanded Brazil's 'capitulation' in tariff negotiations, seeking unrestricted access to sensitive economic sectors without offering equivalent concessions. Brazil rejected the demands, viewing them as one-sided and politically motivated rather than based on fair trade concerns. Vieira noted over 30 meetings since March 2025, including presidential-level talks between Lula and Trump, but no agreement has been reached.

item.title: Leia na íntegra a resposta do Itamaraty ao novo tarifaço de Trump
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira dismissed the Trump administration's justifications for imposing 25% tariffs on Brazilian products, stating they 'have no basis in reality'. He emphasized that Brazil held over 30 meetings with U.S. officials since March 2025 and refused to yield to unreasonable demands. The Lula government plans to invoke the Reciprocity Law to counter the measure, which takes effect on July 22, 2026.

item.title: Governo Lula acredita em motivação política para novo tarifaço
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated that the new U.S. tariffs on Brazil are politically motivated, not commercial, emphasizing that Brazil negotiated in good faith since March 2025 with over 30 meetings at presidential, ministerial, and technical levels. He denounced Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s remarks as 'rude and arrogant' and rejected U.S. demands for unrestricted economic opening without reciprocity, calling them an attempt at 'capitulation'.

item.title: Governo diz que Rubio critica Lula de forma “arrogante e grosseira”
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira accused U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of being 'rude and arrogant' for his criticisms of President Lula following the imposition of a 25% additional tariff on Brazilian goods by the USTR. Vieira called Rubio’s statements unacceptable and offensive, claiming the tariff is politically motivated, not economic, as Brazil refused to yield to unreasonable U.S. demands during over 30 negotiation meetings since March 2025.

item.title: Sem Michelle, campanha de Flávio fará ‘caravana’ feminina para percorrer o país e apresentar propostas às mulheres
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) campaign will launch a women-focused government plan and begin a national caravan to present proposals, led by his wife Fernanda Bolsonaro, Daniella Marques, and Simone Marquetto. The plan includes eliminating daycare waiting lists, creating a voucher for mothers without daycare access, expanding elderly care policies, and promoting female entrepreneurship. The initiative is compared to Michelle Bolsonaro's 2022 strategy, though the campaign avoids labeling it a direct reprise.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro está desesperado com caso Master e age como lobista dos EUA, diz ministro de Lula
item.description: Minister José Guimarães stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro is desperate due to the Banco Master scandal and is acting as a lobbyist for the United States in Brazil. The senator is a pre-candidate for the presidency in 2026.

item.title: Partido questiona no STF regra eleitoral que beneficia filho de Lira, fica sem filiado e ação vira dúvida
item.description: The Christian Democracy party (DC) has filed a direct action of unconstitutionality (ADI 7991) at the STF challenging the 2025 electoral rule that sets different dates to verify minimum age for candidacy, aiming to benefit Alvinho Lira, son of former House Speaker Arthur Lira, who would be 20 at the time of taking office in 2027—below the 21-year minimum for federal deputy. After the filing, Congressman José Carlos Araujo, whose affiliation was used to establish the DC’s standing in the STF, withdrew from the party, leaving it without any congressional representative and jeopardizing its legal standing to maintain the action.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio são orientados a culpar Lula pelo tarifaço nas redes
item.description: Allies of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) are being instructed to use social media to blame the Lula (PT) government for the tariff increase imposed by the United States. The strategy aims to deflect criticism from external trade policies and redirect it toward the Brazilian president, despite the tariff being a unilateral U.S. measure. This reflects an effort to politicize an international economic issue for electoral gain in 2026.

item.title: Moraes manteve Bolsonaro em domiciliar para evitar tensão política
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest rather than returning him to closed regime to avoid political tension and protests, as Bolsonaro could leverage his status to influence the 2026 elections. The decision, grounded in humanitarian reasons following his hospitalization, was seen as politically calculated, given Bolsonaro continues to exert influence through family statements and support for candidates, including his son Flávio. Banker Daniel Vorcaro also indirectly benefited, as he would have been moved from his isolated cell if Bolsonaro were returned to closed custody.

item.title: 'Grosseiro' e 'arrogante': Vieira rebate ataque de Marco Rubio a Lula
item.description: Brazil's Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira condemned statements by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio about President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as 'gross', 'arrogant', and 'unacceptable', saying they offensively targeted the leader of a friendly nation. Vieira also stressed that investigations under Section 301 of U.S. trade law are unilateral actions by the U.S. government and that there is no justification for imposing tariffs on Brazilian goods, reaffirming the importance of bilateral cooperation.

item.title: O que incomoda os EUA é o Brasil não ter se curvado, diz Vieira
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated that the U.S. imposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods because the Lula administration did not yield to President Donald Trump's demands. He said the measure reflects U.S. dissatisfaction with Brazil's independent stance amid commercial pressures. Vieira emphasized that Brazil's refusal to comply was the primary reason for the tariff increase.

item.title: Governo brasileiro fala sobre novo tarifaço de 25% dos EUA
item.description: The Brazilian government convened a ministerial meeting to discuss the new 25% tariff imposed by the United States on industrial and certain agricultural goods, effective July 22. Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira called the measure unjustified and offensive, criticizing statements by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. While oil, coffee, and beef are exempt, sugar, ethanol, and tobacco will be subject to the tariff.

item.title: Tarifaço: Vieira defende Pix e diz que acusação dos EUA é “descabida”
item.description: Brazil's Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira defended the Pix payment system against U.S. allegations of unfair practices, calling the claims 'baseless' and stating that Pix is free and does not harm U.S. competitors. He also dismissed remarks by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio as unacceptable and offensive, asserting that Brazil refused to yield to trade pressure. The U.S. 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, based on a Section 301 investigation, took effect on July 22, citing Pix and illegal deforestation as justifications.

item.title: O impacto da selfie de Flávio Bolsonaro com Sicário nas redes
item.description: The selfie of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro with Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as 'Sicário' and linked to the private militia of the former Banco Master owner, had limited impact on social media, with most of the reaction confined to platform X, according to a Bites consultancy report. The image was shared last Wednesday (15) and generated little engagement outside that environment.

item.title: Vieira classifica como 'ofensivas' declarações de Rubio e diz que secretário dos EUA ataca Lula com grosseria e arrogância
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira denounced U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's remarks as unacceptable and offensive to the Brazilian people, stating that Rubio attacked President Lula with grossness and arrogance. Vieira said Rubio's criticisms followed the U.S. announcement of 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods and reflected Washington's discomfort with Brazil's refusal to yield to unreasonable demands in negotiations.

item.title: Nexus: foto de Flávio com Sicário engajou mais que tarifaço nas redes
item.description: The photo of Flávio Bolsonaro alongside Daniel Vorcaro's 'Sicário' generated 1,247,615 social media interactions between July 15 and 16, exceeding by 22% the engagement of the U.S. tariff announcement on Brazilian products (1,020,184 interactions). The highest engagement came from Instagram (48%), followed by Facebook (29%) and X (23%). PL leaders claim they had knowledge of the image for over a month.

item.title: Mauro Vieira diz que novas tarifas dos EUA não têm justificativa: 'Motivação política e tentativa de interferência no Judiciário'
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated that the new 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods lack justification and are politically motivated, aiming to interfere in Brazil's judiciary. He emphasized that Brazil has pursued dialogue since before 2025 and deemed the measures unacceptable, particularly as they target national economic sectors under U.S. demands. The tariffs, set to take effect on July 22, stem from a year-long Section 301 investigation by the USTR.

item.title: Mauro Vieira faz pronunciamento sobre tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira condemned the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, calling Secretary of State Marco Rubio's statements 'unacceptable and offensive'. He affirmed that the Lula administration negotiated in good faith and that the U.S. measures stem from a USTR investigation alleging unfair Brazilian trade practices, including the Pix payment system and illegal deforestation.

item.title: Tarifaço: Rubio ataca Lula de forma grosseira em declarações inaceitáveis, diz Mauro Vieira
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira strongly criticized U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's statements, calling them 'gross and arrogant' attacks on President Lula that are 'unacceptable'. Vieira emphasized Lula’s efforts to engage in dialogue with the U.S., noting 11 contacts with American officials, and denounced the 25% tariff on Brazilian goods as unilateral, illegal, and arbitrary, stating Brazil will invoke the Reciprocity Law and bring the matter to the WTO.

item.title: PF abre linha de investigação sobre elo entre Dark Horse e PCC
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating a possible link between the film Dark Horse, a biopic of Jair Bolsonaro, and ACX ITC Tecnologia, a company tied to the PCC, after discovering R$ 28 million was transferred from Entre Investimentos e Participações — used by Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film — to ACX ITC between February and April 2025. The PF is examining whether part of the R$ 134 million agreement between Vorcaro and Flávio Bolsonaro was diverted for money laundering, analyzing banking and fiscal secrecy breaches of Entre.

item.title: TSE manda derrubar vídeo de canal de esquerda que ligava Flávio ao PCC
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques ordered the immediate removal of a video from the left-wing channel Plantão Brasil that accused Flávio Bolsonaro of ties to the PCC, ruling it as negative anticipatory election propaganda and disinformation. The decision followed a lawsuit by Bolsonaro's Liberal Party, giving 24 hours to remove the content under threat of fine, as the video falsely attributes proven crimes to the senator without evidence.
